title: Refit a bakery mixer beater and verify a guarded start and stop
instruction: Fit the clean flat beater to the stopped bakery mixer: align its slotted hub, push it onto the shaft against the spring-loaded collar, turn it into the retaining pocket and release it. Seat the guard on the lowered bowl, raise the bowl with the lift handle, then run the mixer at its preset low speed for at least five seconds and switch it off. Leave both hands clear, the beater secured and the guard fitted.
context: Fitting the clean flat beater after washing is a familiar part of preparing cake or cookie batter in a stand mixer. The installed bowl and fixed head constrain the approach: the robot must align the hub with a partly obscured pin, maintain spring compression while turning, and leave the tool hanging securely before the guarded start-and-stop check.
setup: Simulation inventory and rendered materials follow; PHYSICAL_BUILD.md specifies the alternative printed empty-bowl apparatus, its full-size geometry, target masses and material/drive/support differences. One fixed generic compact bench mixer: painted steel chassis with a 310 x 280 mm base, approximately 475 mm high; stainless bowl 232 mm across its outer rim and 142 mm deep, already mounted and clamped, empty and lowered. Painted steel external lift cradle: 18 x 255 x 18 mm rear bar, two 130 x 20 x 12 mm side arms and 20 x 20 x 25 mm trunnion risers. One 250 g aluminium flat beater, 109 mm wide and 195 mm high, with a 12.7 mm hub bore around a 12 mm shaft and a 4 mm drive pin. A 20 g stainless retaining collar (32 mm outside diameter, 18 mm bore, 1.5 mm thick) has 8 mm axial travel and a native spring with 5 N preload, 400 N/m stiffness and 4 N s/m damping. One 180 g stainless wire guard, approximately 216 x 261 x 62 mm including its polymer grip tab, supported 28 mm above the guard rim. Polymer draining supports: beater base 130 x 130 x 15 mm with retaining rails, and guard platform 260 x 250 x 20 mm. Manual lift handle with a rubber knob, 75 mm bowl travel; green START and red STOP polymer buttons, 4 mm travel. Wooden work surface 1100 x 1300 x 60 mm, top at 747.5 mm. Mixer base origin (350, 30, 747.5) mm; beater hub initially (240, 320, 987) mm before settling; guard rim origin (450, 310, 782.5) mm before settling. All initial orientations are identity. Both robot hands start open in READY. Robot bases: (0, +/-305, 750) mm. Coordinates: x forward, y left, z up. geometry.json gives all colliders; setup.png shows the settled layout.
scoring: Observable stages, judged with a ruler, external reference marks and continuous timed video: 0.25 for one second of released beater hanging in its external working band, with bowl lowered and guard at least 350 mm from the hub; 0.50 additionally for a guard seated and released for one second with the bowl at its upper mark; 0.75 additionally for five uninterrupted seconds of motor-driven clockwise beater rotation at one revolution per second or faster with both hands clear; 1.00 after STOP and a two-second motor-off, hands-clear endpoint with at most 5 degrees total visible beater/carrier travel. The exposed beater neck reference is 40 mm below its origin: within 5 mm horizontally and 10 mm vertically of its mounted reference, upright within 10 degrees. Guard reference: within 5 mm horizontally and vertically, level within 5 degrees and orientation within 10 degrees; bowl within 5 mm of its lower/upper mark. Released beater clearance is greater than 75 mm from each marked gripper centre to the centreline at the hub and 40, 105 and 170 mm below it; released guard clearance is greater than 190 mm from each gripper centre to its centre. No internal hub yaw, spring travel, contact flag, hidden shaft speed or exact drive ratio decides a stage. Dropping/removing the beater cancels its retention proof; guard removal or bowl lowering cancels the powered interval. The score falls to the currently valid stage. Workspace exit, hand intrusion into the rotating-bowl cylinder, or guard/bowl disengagement during powered/coasting motion above 5 rpm latches zero. Alteration, damage or added props also invalidates a physical trial. PHYSICAL_SCORING.md defines the references, workspace, exclusion cylinder, observation procedure and boundary conventions; all bands are inclusive unless stated greater than or strictly between.
reset_notes: No consumables. Stop the apparatus, lower and empty the bowl, and return the guard and beater to their supports. Reset motor, button and scoring state. In simulation, recreate and settle the fixed scene before beginning the control budget.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX at 960 Hz. Full-size pin/L-slot, spring collar, bowl and guard/lift are retained. OEM-inspired geometry/forces are assumed. The unbuilt ~$353 printed/ballasted build changes hidden supports, extends the nose cover 12 mm lower, and puts beater COM ~110 vs modeled 80 mm below hub. Inertia, friction and damping are approximate. Exterior marks/visible motion score; precise predicates only interlock START. Food, deformation and electrical faults are omitted.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (3,600 controls; manual endpoint-video rescore of the original native trial). Uploaded scripted demo: 1.0 (3,540 controls; revised rubric applied to its saved native trace). A fresh native run of the revised scorer also reached 1.0 in 3,540 controls; see fresh-native-validation.json. No new model inference is claimed.
